History:
• Chief complaint: Progressive shortness of breath.  
• Onset/duration: Began insidiously ≈2 weeks ago; significantly worse over the last few days.  
• Character/progression: Now breathless with minimal exertion (e.g., walking to shops, around house); requires rest to catch breath.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild dry cough, new bilateral ankle swelling for “last few days,” feeling slightly run-down.  
• Negative symptoms: Denies chest pain, palpitations, fever, appetite change, or urinary change (other than historically increased frequency on diuretics).  
• Prior episodes: Similar swelling when heart failure first diagnosed.  
• Triggers/relievers: Not specified.  
• Concerns: Fear that heart failure is worsening and may affect ability to work (lorry driver).

Past Medical History:
• Congestive heart failure (date not specified).  
• “Small heart attack”/probable myocardial infarction ≈5 years ago (hospitalized a few days).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medications:  
  – Furosemide – dose/route/frequency not documented (currently once daily; plan to ↑ to twice daily).  
  – Aspirin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  – Bisoprolol – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: None reported.  
• Family history: Father died of heart attack in early 60s; mother alive with osteoporosis.  
• Social: Lives alone with two cats; part-time lorry driver (day shifts). Ex-smoker (≈1 pack/day × 25 yrs, quit date not given). No alcohol. Light daily walking for exercise.

Physical Examination:
• General: Patient conversing normally via teleconsult, reports increased breathlessness.  
• Chest: Stated by clinician to be clear; oxygen saturation and blood pressure “OK” (exact values not provided).  
• Extremities: Patient-reported bilateral ankle edema.  
• Mental status: Alert and oriented.  
• No throat swelling; no signs of acute distress reported.

Impression:
Acute decompensation/exacerbation of known congestive heart failure.

Management Plan:
• Pharmacologic: Increase Furosemide to 1 tablet twice daily for a few days, then reassess (exact dose not documented).  
• Investigations:  
  – Blood tests: full blood count, renal function, others as per heart failure panel.  
  – Echocardiogram to reassess cardiac function (to be arranged within 1–2 weeks).  
• Follow-up: Review in 1 week; earlier if worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.  
• Safety-net advice: Contact clinic or emergency services immediately for acute deterioration.

Patient Summary:
Mr. Oscar presents with 2 weeks of progressively worsening dyspnea and new ankle edema. Findings are most consistent with a heart-failure flare-up. Diuretic dose is being increased, blood work and repeat echocardiogram arranged, and he will be reviewed in one week.

Key Takeaways:
1. Start taking Furosemide twice daily instead of once daily until reviewed.  
2. Attend for blood tests and scheduled echocardiogram.  
3. Seek urgent help for new chest pain, rapid heartbeat, marked breathlessness, or dizziness.

Next Steps:
• Complete ordered labs and imaging.  
• Reassess symptoms and fluid status at 1-week follow-up.  
• Adjust long-term heart-failure regimen based on test results and clinical response.
